items.title: NVIDIA Dynamo Encode-Prefill-Decode disaggregation
items.why_now: NVIDIA has published an implementation and workload guidance for separating multimodal encode from LLM prefill/decode.
items.test_plan: Instrument encode, prefill and decode separately on representative image-heavy VLM traffic; compare aggregated serving versus EPD with identical model, prompts and concurrency.
success_criteria: Material p95 TTFT improvement
Higher goodput at equal or lower cost
No meaningful increase in errors or transfer overhead
risks: Vendor benchmark results may not generalize
Decode-heavy or dense-model workloads may see little benefit

items.title: DeepSeek V4.1-Flash
items.why_now: A new Flash release is being reported with claims of higher throughput and faster inference, but decision-grade technical documentation is still incomplete in this research set.
items.test_plan: Run a fixed internal 20-50 task suite with the same harness as the current baseline and record task success, p50/p95 latency, tool/schema errors, tokens and cost per successful task.
success_criteria: Statistically meaningful task-success/cost or task-success/latency improvement on the target workload
Stable documented API/model identity
No regression in tool use or structured output reliability
risks: Current performance claims are vendor claims

items.title: Policy gate for persistent agent-memory writes
items.why_now: MemSentry provides a concrete security model for treating persistent memory writes as privileged state transitions rather than ordinary data writes.
items.test_plan: Place a non-production gate before persistent memory writes and evaluate source trust, semantic risk, access/permission impact and blast radius across a small poisoning test corpus.
success_criteria: Known malicious writes are quarantined/reviewed
Benign memory writes retain acceptable false-positive rate
Every decision has provenance and is auditable
risks: Published evidence is synthetic and not independently replicated
Semantic classifiers may not transfer to domain-specific memory

items.title: Internal agent registry with delegated authority
items.why_now: Payment ecosystems are converging on explicit agent identity and registries, making the pattern directly testable inside enterprise agent systems.
items.test_plan: Register 3-5 internal agents with stable IDs, principal/owner, allowed capabilities, policy version, expiry and revocation; require registry lookup plus external policy check before irreversible actions.
success_criteria: Every irreversible action maps to agent, principal and active delegation
Revoked agents lose access without prompt changes
Credential material stays outside the agent runtime
risks: Registry state does not itself stop prompt injection
Poor lifecycle management can create stale authority

items.title: Hermetic coding-agent canary for untrusted repositories
items.why_now: The Beltdown disclosure shows that sandboxing model-issued shell commands is insufficient when harness-owned Git or tooling can execute outside the sandbox.
items.test_plan: Open a harmless adversarial repository fixture inside a disposable coding-agent environment and verify that agent, harness, Git, indexers and build tools cannot affect host processes/files, reach credential sockets or bypass controlled network egress.
success_criteria: No host filesystem/process effects
No access to host SSH/cloud credential material
All network egress is mediated and auditable
Artifacts leave only through an explicit export path
risks: One canary cannot cover every IDE/plugin/harness path
Isolation that is strong on one OS may not transfer to another
items.maturity: experimental security validation pattern based on a primary vulnerability disclosure; production coverage depends on harness topology

items.title: Cost-per-successful-outcome model benchmark harness
items.why_now: AWS/OpenAI published a reproducible harness that measures task correctness and agent trajectory economics instead of only token price, matching the project's task-success-per-cost evaluation principle.
items.test_plan: Replace the published tasks with 50-100 representative internal tasks, pin prompts and model parameters, define a binary/graded quality gate, and record task success, total turns, latency, tokens, review/rework and cost per passing task.
success_criteria: Model ranking is stable across repeated runs
Task-success/cost differences are large enough to affect routing or model choice
Reasoning settings and provider harnesses are configuration-equivalent for any direct comparison
risks: The published AWS comparison uses non-equivalent reasoning settings for some models
LLM judging can bias correctness unless calibrated against human labels
items.maturity: trial methodology; open-source harness is available but published rankings should not be treated as intrinsic model capability

items.title: Dual-layer production monitoring for agents
items.why_now: AWS published a concrete reference architecture that separates agent outcome quality from infrastructure health, reducing the risk of treating successful API calls as successful agent work.
items.test_plan: Instrument one agent workflow with two independent channels: infrastructure signals such as IAM/throttling/tool/network failures, and outcome signals such as goal success, response correctness and tool-trajectory quality. Inject one failure in each layer separately.
success_criteria: A healthy-infrastructure/bad-outcome incident is detected by the quality layer
A good-plan/broken-infrastructure incident is detected by the operations layer
Both alerts point to distinct remediation paths
risks: Sampling may miss rare failure modes
Reference architecture is AWS-specific even though the pattern is portable
items.maturity: watch-to-trial reference pattern with available implementation guidance
